questions.questionText: Consider the pushdown automaton (PDA) P below, which runs on the input alpha- bet {a, b}, has stack alphabet {, A}, and has three states {s, p, q}, with s being the start state. A transition from state u to state v, labelled c/X/, where c is an input symbol or , X is a stack symbol, and is a string of stack symbols, represents the fact that in state u, the PDA can read c from the input, with X on the top of its stack, pop X from the stack, push in the string on the stack, and go to state v. In the initial configuration, the stack has only the symbol in it. The PDA accepts by empty stack. a//A b/A/ a/A/AA s b/A/ p /A/ /A/ q /A/ // Which one of the following options correctly describes the language accepted by P ?
questions.explanation: Each 'a' pushes an A onto the stack (first a pushes the initial A, subsequent a's duplicate the top A, effectively adding one A per a). Each 'b' pops an A. The stack is emptied exactly when the number of b's equals the number of a's, so the PDA accepts the language {aⁿbⁿ | n ≥ 0}.

questions.questionText: Consider a disk with the following specifications: rotation speed of 6000 RPM, average seek time of 5 milliseconds, 500 sectors/track, 512-byte sectors. A file has content stored in 3000 sectors located randomly on the disk. Assuming average rotational latency, the total time (in seconds, rounded off to 2 decimal places) to read the entire file from the disk is _________
questions.explanation: Each random sector requires average seek (5 ms) + average rotational latency (half of 10 ms = 5 ms) + transfer time (10 ms per revolution / 500 sectors = 0.02 ms). Total per sector ≈ 10.02 ms = 0.01002 s. For 3000 sectors: 3000 × 0.01002 s ≈ 30.06 s, rounded to two decimal places.

questions.questionText: Consider sending an IP datagram of size 1420 bytes (including 20 bytes of IP header) from a sender to a receiver over a path of two links with a router between them. The first link (sender to router) has an MTU (Maximum Transmission Unit) size of 542 bytes, while the second link (router to receiver) has an MTU size of 360 bytes. The number of fragments that would be delivered at the receiver is ________
questions.explanation: The original 1400‑byte payload is first fragmented on the 542‑byte MTU link into three pieces of 520, 520 and 360 bytes of data. On the second link (MTU 360), each of these fragments is further split into sub‑fragments with a maximum data size of 336 bytes (multiple of 8). Thus 520 → 336+184 (2 fragments), another 520 → 336+184 (2 fragments), and 360 → 336+24 (2 fragments). Total fragments received = 2+2+2 = 6.

questions.questionText: Let be an undirected connected graph in which every edge has a positive integer weight. Suppose that every spanning tree in has even weight. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE for every such graph ?
options: All edges in have even weight
All edges in have even weight OR all edges in have odd weight
In each cycle in , all edges in have even weight
In each cycle in , either all edges in have even weight OR all edges in
questions.explanation: Let O be the set of odd‑weight edges. For any spanning tree T, the condition that its total weight is even means |T∩O| is even. If we take an edge e∉T and add it to T, we obtain a unique cycle C = T+e. Replacing any edge f of C by e yields another spanning tree T' = T−f+e, which must also have an even number of odd edges. Hence parity(e)=parity(f) for every f∈C. Therefore all edges of any cycle have the same parity (all even or all odd). This proves statement D. Statements A, B and C are not necessary; counter‑examples exist (e.g., a graph where all edges are odd and the number of vertices is odd satisfies the premise but violates A and B, and a graph consisting of two cycles, one all even and one all odd, satisfies the premise but violates C and B).
